comparison: Perfect agreement on claims C24, C78, C79 regarding pH-dependent tag effects on activity. Both evaluations find these observations supported without criticism.

Both address mutagenesis claims C20-C23, C41 about N160 residue. OpenEval finds the data clearly supportive with functional assays confirming electroneutrality. Peer reviewers accept the findings as valid but note they are 'unsurprising' and limited in scope.

Strong disagreement on claims C48, C51, C52 regarding temperature extrapolation. OpenEval finds the extrapolation reasonable based on structural similarity. Peer reviewers explicitly reject this as 'misleading speculation' and call the 500,000 ions/second estimate unrealistic.

Significant disagreement on EM structure determination (C29-C31, C33-C34). OpenEval finds the EM data well-documented with appropriate quality metrics. Peer reviewers express major concerns, stating methods are 'poorly justified' and the outward-open assignment is 'not convincing' due to limited resolution in the vertical direction.

Agreement on x-ray structure claims C2, C32 (inward-open state). Both evaluations accept the structural determination. Peer reviewer R1 also addresses C10, C13, C53 which OpenEval covers in separate results.

Disagreement on rocking bundle mechanism (C6, C66, C72). OpenEval finds the mechanistic model well-supported by structural comparisons and functional data. Peer reviewers question the validity because it depends on the questionable EM structure assignment.

Disagreement on detailed transport mechanism (C67-C71). OpenEval supports the mechanistic model based on structural states. Peer reviewers find it uncertain because it depends on the unconvincing outward-open EM structure assignment.

Disagreement on pH-dependent activity measurements (C5, C25-C26, C45-C46). OpenEval finds the 22Na+ uptake data systematic and reproducible. Peer reviewers criticize the acridine orange assay methodology, stating it's qualitative only and 'relative rates as a function of pH in Figure 5 are unreliable.'

Disagreement on kinetic parameters (C27-C28, C47). OpenEval accepts the Km and vmax values from Figure 5C. Peer reviewers state 'data does not seem to be approaching saturation' and therefore kinetic parameters are unreliable.

Agreement on lack of pH-induced conformational changes (C55-C57). Both evaluations support this finding. Peer reviewers explicitly call this 'a useful finding' and note the similarity between active MjNhaP and inactive PaNhaP structures argues against large pH-induced changes.

Agreement on H1 deletion mutagenesis (C11, C17). OpenEval finds the deletion mutants demonstrate functional requirements. Peer reviewers accept these findings without challenge, though noting mutagenesis studies are minimal overall.
Agreement on topology determination (C12). OpenEval supports the PhoA/GFP topology assays. Peer reviewers raise no concerns about this standard methodological approach.

Partial overlap on pH profile (C45-C46). OpenEval supports the pH-dependent activity interpretation. Peer reviewers question the underlying acridine orange assay methodology for quantitative pH measurements.

Disagreement on projection difference analysis and rocking bundle (C65, C75-C76). OpenEval finds the difference maps support the mechanism. Peer reviewers find this uncertain because it depends on the questionable EM structure assignment.

Disagreement on structural comparisons to other antiporters (C35-C36). OpenEval finds the similarity to TtNapA and ASBT provides independent validation. Peer reviewers question the validity of structural comparisons due to concerns about the EM structure.

Disagreement on broad conclusions about antiporter mechanisms (C38, C43-C44). OpenEval finds these generalizations reasonably supported by available structural data. Peer reviewers find them uncertain, noting 'the overall significance of the high pH structure alone is not compelling.'
Agreement on H1 functional role (C14-C15). Both evaluations support these findings about H1's requirement for function based on mutagenesis data.

Disagreement on turnover rate and temperature extrapolation (C48-C50). OpenEval finds the turnover calculation straightforward and temperature extrapolation reasonable. Peer reviewers explicitly reject the high-temperature estimate as unrealistic.
OpenEval supports background/context claims C1, C9 about biological significance. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these introductory claims.
OpenEval supports claim C16 about dimerization vs function based on cited literature. No corresponding peer review evaluation found.
OpenEval supports claim C73 as reasonable speculation about future research directions. No corresponding peer review evaluation found.

OpenEval supports physiological mechanism claims C58-C64 based on structural and functional data. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for this specific set of claims about competitive binding and pH-dependent ion exchange.
